top_categories.workout_context: Race-pace efforts that mimic GFNY Bahamas' demands. Pacing, fueling, and tactical decisions under fatigue. Practice the race before November.

Road-specific control matters at GFNY Bahamas. Practice on flat: use smooth gear and cadence changes, accelerate deliberately out of corners, and settle quickly back into sustainable power for 60 miles.
When someone attacks on flat, you have 10 seconds to respond or you're off the back. This builds that response.
60 miles on flat burns energy faster than the distance suggests. Train the fade resistance now.
GFNY Bahamas' flat rewards steady threshold power. Surging and recovering costs more watts than just holding.
88–92% FTP is where you'll spend the hardest sustained miles of GFNY Bahamas. Train it until it feels boring.
At GFNY Bahamas, changes in grade or pace can lift effort above threshold before it settles again. Over-unders train that transition while you keep riding.
2-minute all-out efforts on flat. Closing gaps, responding to attacks, sprinting for position. Train the burn.
Brief efforts above sustainable power can come from grade changes, positioning, or closing a gap at GFNY Bahamas. Train them without letting those efforts derail the longer pacing plan.
Long rides with hard efforts mixed in. Simulates what GFNY Bahamas' flat actually does to you.
Double-threshold training builds sustained power with less fatigue. More FTP per hour of training.
Varied gradients on flat demand climbing versatility. Sit the shallow stuff, stand the steep stuff, switch without thinking.

pack_summary: This 10-workout pack focuses on Race Simulation, Road Specific, and VO2max to prepare you for 60 miles of flat in West Bay Street near Goodman's Bay Park, Nassau, New Providence Island, The Bahamas.
